steps.aria:
- main:
  - heading "Connect your coding agent" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Paste one line into a terminal (a shell, not your agent's chat). Pasting it is your yes to adding Foundry. Foundry doesn't change your agent's settings for you.
  - heading "What your agent can and can't do with Foundry" [level=2]
  - list:
    - listitem: Draft an automation from what you ask for.
    - listitem: Test it with pretend data.
    - listitem: "It can't turn anything on through Foundry: you do."
    - listitem: "It can't approve what an automation makes through Foundry: you do, in a dialog or in this page. An agent allowed to run any command as you could; see How this is kept safe."
  - heading "Claude Code Preview" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "In a terminal, inside the project where you'll use Foundry:"
  - text: claude mcp add --transport stdio foundry -- "/opt/node24/bin/node" "/home/user/workflow-foundry/.claude/worktrees/wf_c7946468-203-16/app/cli.mjs" mcp --dashboard --consent --workspace "/tmp/journey-p1-cursor-codex-XwyNoJ"
  - button "Copy"
  - paragraph: "Or, for every project:"
  - text: claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio foundry -- "/opt/node24/bin/node" "/home/user/workflow-foundry/.claude/worktrees/wf_c7946468-203-16/app/cli.mjs" mcp --dashboard --consent --workspace "/tmp/journey-p1-cursor-codex-XwyNoJ"
  - button "Copy"
  - paragraph: "Then start claude there and type /mcp: foundry should show as connected. Claude Code always asks you before ask_person_to_turn_on runs. Other Foundry tools may run without asking, depending on your permission mode (in auto mode, a classifier reviews tool calls instead of asking you). Tested with a scripted client, not yet with a released Claude Code."
  - group: "▸ Optional: let your agent draft and test without asking each time. Add these names to permissions, allow, in your Claude Code settings:"
  - heading "Cursor Preview" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "Add this to .cursor/mcp.json in your project, or to your user settings:"
  - text: "{ \"mcpServers\": { \"foundry\": { \"command\": \"/opt/node24/bin/node\", \"args\": [ \"/home/user/workflow-foundry/.claude/worktrees/wf_c7946468-203-16/app/cli.mjs\", \"mcp\", \"--dashboard\", \"--consent\", \"--workspace\", \"/tmp/journey-p1-cursor-codex-XwyNoJ\" ] } } }"
  - button "Copy"
  - paragraph: "Or use a one-click link (built from Cursor's documented format; not yet tried in Cursor): Preview"
  - text: cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=foundry&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoiL29wdC9ub2RlMjQvYmluL25vZGUiLCJhcmdzIjpbIi9ob21lL3VzZXIvd29ya2Zsb3ctZm91bmRyeS8uY2xhdWRlL3dvcmt0cmVlcy93Zl9jNzk0NjQ2OC0yMDMtMTYvYXBwL2NsaS5tanMiLCJtY3AiLCItLWRhc2hib2FyZCIsIi0tY29uc2VudCIsIi0td29ya3NwYWNlIiwiL3RtcC9qb3VybmV5LXAxLWN1cnNvci1jb2RleC1Yd3lOb0oiXX0=
  - button "Copy"
  - paragraph: "Cursor shows you the server before it adds it. Foundry asks for your decisions in your browser, not in Cursor's own dialog: it can't look for hooks in Cursor that could answer that dialog for you. Tested with a scripted client, not yet in Cursor."
  - heading "Codex Preview" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "In a terminal:"
  - text: codex mcp add foundry -- "/opt/node24/bin/node" "/home/user/workflow-foundry/.claude/worktrees/wf_c7946468-203-16/app/cli.mjs" mcp --dashboard --consent --workspace "/tmp/journey-p1-cursor-codex-XwyNoJ"
  - button "Copy"
  - paragraph: "Codex documents a setting that lets an MCP server's dialog reach you (approval_policy.granular.mcp_elicitations in its config reference, read 2026-10-21); with it off, Codex turns the dialog down by itself. Tested with a scripted client, not yet with a released Codex."

    - /url: "#/connect-agent"

steps.aria:
- main:
  - heading "Waiting for you (1)" [level=1]
  - paragraph:
    - text: "You decide here, in your terminal, or in your coding agent's dialog. Foundry's tools can't decide for you. Nothing real is made or sent until you say yes. Tests on pretend data and new versions are made without asking you. The limit: a coding agent that can run commands as you on this computer could do what you can do, including say yes. Works now (Our own tests of this site and its tools. Not covered: any program running as you on this computer.)"
    - 'link "Source: Nothing real happens until you say yes (with one honest limit)"':
      - /url: "#/claims?claim=C01"
      - text: (source)
  - article "Turn on 'Invoice reminders' (version 1)?":
    - heading "Turn on 'Invoice reminders' (version 1)?" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Each run, draft an e-mail to every customer whose open invoice is overdue the reminder its age calls for (a friendly reminder once an invoice is 7 days late, a second reminder at 14 days, a final notice at 30 days), never twice for the same stage, after a person approves the full list.
    - heading "Steps" [level=3]
    - list:
      - listitem: Read the invoices sheet
      - listitem: Keep open invoices only (not paid, not disputed)
      - listitem: Work out how many days late each open invoice is
      - listitem: Decide which reminder each invoice is due for
      - listitem: Keep the invoices due for a reminder
      - listitem: Remind each customer once per stage
      - listitem: List the reminder drafts this run made
      - listitem: Who should get a reminder draft this run
      - listitem: List the invoices due for a reminder
      - listitem: Write the summary
      - listitem: Draft the summary to me@example.com (you see it first)
      - listitem: "Re-read the drafts: exactly the planned e-mails were written this run, word for word"
    - heading "How you'll know it worked" [level=3]
    - list:
      - listitem: "Passed: Every late, open invoice got the reminder its lateness calls for, or already had it"
      - listitem: "Passed: Exactly the planned reminders were drafted, word for word (checked by re-reading the drafts)"
      - listitem: "Passed: The summary for me@example.com was drafted"
      - listitem: "Passed: Re-read the drafts: exactly the planned e-mails were written this run, word for word"
    - paragraph: Ticks come from the test with pretend data.
    - button "Turn it on"
    - button "No"
